To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel kinematic structure of a robotic exoskeleton for human arm rehabilitation was developed and tested.
the design of a wearable exoskeleton for upper limb rehabilitation can be optimized for comfort and usability by applying kinematic design principles.
a novel kinematic paradigm can be used to design exoskeletons for ergonomic human machine interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new paradigm for the design of kinematic structures for ergonomic human-robot interaction, and its application in the design of a novel upper-arm exoskeletal rehabilitation robot.
the design of a kinematic structure for a human-machine interface that allows a high degree of interaction between a human limb and a machine.
the design of human machine interfaces, which are able to interact with the human arm over the entire workspace, while not being limited to the human joint centers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach can be applied successfully to the design of human machine interfaces, such as exoskeletons and prostheses, and can lead to significant improvements in the ergonomics of the human machine interaction.

the presented kinematic design paradigm enables the design of a wide range of human-machine interfaces, that are able to interact with the natural human limb kinematics, without requiring alignment to the limb.

we have developed a kinematic design paradigm, that is capable of producing exoskeletons for human arm interfacing, that can interact with an almost complete portion of the human arm’s workspace, including shoulder-girdle motion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented design paradigm is able to generate a kinematic structure that is optimal for human-machine interaction in terms of ergonomics.
a kinematic design approach for ergonomic human machine interface can be formulated and implemented in a novel kinematic structure.

the presented design paradigm is a generic approach for the design of kinematic structures in human machine interaction that is based on the kinematics of the human limb, that can be used to create kinematic structures for human machine interaction that are comfortable to wear, do not require alignment, and are able to interact with the entire natural workspace of the human limb.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinematic design of the exoskeletal device has a strong impact on its ergonomics, usability and effectiveness.
the design of kinematic structures for human machine interaction can be formulated generically and optimized using the kinematics of the human body.
the design of a kinematic structure for an arm interfacing device is not a trivial problem, but requires a systematic approach.
